There are several things that really helped me quick cold turkey nine years ago. I hope they help you.

One is knowing that the urges are only about 5 seconds long. Of course when you first stop smoking the urges might only be a few minutes apart but the urges really do go away within about 5 seconds. Don't dwell on it to make it last more than that. Just let it go.

Another one that helped me was to not focus on how miserable I am not smoking. This was the biggest hurdle for me the hundreds if not thousands of times I tried to quit and failed. I had this "poor me" attitude. "I'm so miserable. If I was smoking I wouldn't feel this bad". You're sense of smell increases ten fold. When I would first quit smoking I could smell someone smoking a mile away. I would focus on how lucky he or she was to not feel as miserable as me. I can't tell you how many times I failed with this kind of attitude.

However, the biggest thing that helped me finally quit was a part from the book "The easy way to quit smoking" by Alan Carr. I've spoken with several people who quit smoking by reading this book and everyone seemed to get a different part of the book that helped them. Mine was where Alan talked about people think they enjoy smoking. I told myself that many, many times. The fact is though smokers don't enjoy smoking. When you crave a cigarette you're miserable. When you light up another one, the misery goes away. I don't know if this helps you or not (I hope it does) but it was tremendous on helping me finally quit once I realized that I didn't smoke because I liked it. In fact I have never in my life met one smoker that was glad that they smoke. I only smoked to make the pain go away which gave me a false security.

I really do wish you the best of luck. I know the uneasiness you're going through, but hang in there. It really, really, truly does get better and easier the longer you're not smoking.
